# 4 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Mother's Speech Recalled

---

**1** If therefore a woman who was old and spiritually widowed, who had borne seven sons, could endure watching them all tortured to death, then it must be acknowledged beyond all doubt that devout reason is sovereign over the passions.

**2** I have thus demonstrated that not only men have exercised reason over the passions,

**3** but that even a woman despised the greatest sufferings. The lions that surrounded Daniel were not so fierce, and the burning furnace of Mishael was not so terrifyingly hot,

**4** as the maternal longing she felt for her seven sons; and yet she watched them all die.

**5** Through reason rooted in religion, the mother quenched passions so overwhelming and so numerous.

**6** Think about this: if this woman had been weak of soul, as a mother might be, she would have mourned over them and perhaps spoken words like these:

**7** Oh how wretched I am! I bore seven sons and now I am the mother of none.

**8** O seven pregnancies, all for nothing! O seven months of labor and exhaustion, all in vain!

**9** For nothing did I nurse you, my sons; wasted were all those months of suckling; in vain I suffered for you the pains of childbirth,

**10** and even greater pains in your upbringing, and greatest of all in your agonizing deaths.

**11** Not one of my sons will close my eyes; not one will lay me in my grave.

**12** But this blessed and holy woman, keeping her reason firm, spoke not one of these words.

**13** She did not weep or wail or say anything unworthy of herself; she did not surrender to grief.

**14** Instead, she urged each of her sons forward to his death for the sake of piety.

**15** O mother, faithful soldier of God! O venerable elder, mighty in battle! O woman stronger than all the men!

**16** You endured watching your children die for piety; you gave your whole family to God!

**17** Was it not you, mother of those sons, who urged each one on his way to martyrdom and called out to each of them by name?

**18** You said to each of them: My son, do not run from the contest; and through me you offered them all as an offering to God.

**19** O mother who surpassed all women in courage! O mother of seven children, most noble and most blessed!

**20** For what mother has ever watched seven sons die in a single day and been so full of the spirit of devotion to God as to urge them all toward death in this way?

**21** Through your holy sons, O mother, you proved that reason is the sovereign master of the passions.

**22** For these sons of yours swept out the ungodly Antiochus like a wind and a tide through the force of their reason and piety.

**23** There are none like them anywhere in human memory, neither men nor women, who overcame the passions so completely.
